 Croatia beats Czechia as Modrić equals Messi
 by croatiaweek 
 November 15, 2026 
 in 
 Sport 
 Ivan PerišIć and Luka Modrić celebrate Croatia’s opener
 Croatia ended a difficult run of results with a victory over Czechia in Osijek on Sunday, securing third place in their UEFA Nations League group and a place in the play-offs to remain in the competition’s top tier. 
 An early goal from Ivan Perišić, and a late winner from substitute Lovro Majer proved decisive as Croatia claimed a 2-1 win at Opus Arena, bringing an end to a four-match losing streak that had marked a first in the national team’s history. 
 The match also saw captain Luka Modrić make his 208th international appearance, drawing level with Lionel Messi. 
 Only Portugal captain Cristiano Ronaldo, with 234 appearances, remains ahead of the 41-year-old. 
 Croatia came into the match under pressure following four consecutive defeats, making the final Group A3 fixture a crucial contest. Third place would secure a place in the play-offs for survival in League A, as well as seeding status in the qualifying campaign for the European Championship. 
 Slaven Bilić’s side made the perfect start in Osijek, taking the lead after just two minutes. 
 Mateo Kovačić drove forward through the middle before finding Dion Drena Beljo. The striker showed good composure to get away from the Czech defenders before laying the ball off to Perišić, who finished accurately from the edge of the penalty area. 
 Croatia continued to look dangerous and had a major opportunity to double their advantage before half-time. 
 Following a corner from Modrić, Luka Vušković headed the ball across goal towards Beljo, who found himself unmarked just four to five metres from the net. However, the striker failed to make proper contact with the ball, allowing Czech goalkeeper Antonín Kinský to make the save. 
 Czechia had periods of possession and threatened through Idris Hopi and Adam Hložek, but Croatia went into the break with their one-goal advantage intact. 
 The hosts continued to create opportunities after the interval. In the 61st minute, Kovačić combined with Petar Sučić in a neat one-two that opened up the Czech defence, but his low effort from around 10 metres was directed straight at Kinský, who made another important save. 
 Croatia had been the more threatening side for much of the contest and created the clearer opportunities, but in the 84th minute Czechia would level through Hložek when his shot from the edge of the box sailed past Dominiik Livaković in goal. 
 Croatia would restore their lead within minutes when Majer, who earned a recall to the national team after missing the World Cup, received the ball in the box, turned and fired off a shot which would find the bottom corner of the net to make it 2-1.
 The victory was an important one for coach Slaven Bilić following a difficult start to his second spell in charge.  
 Croatia will now head into home and away playoffs as third-placed side in the group to stay in League A. Those matches will be played in March 2027 with their opponents revealed next week.
 Starting line-ups: 
 CROATIA: Livaković – Stanišić, Vušković, Ćaleta-Car, Gvardiol – Modrić, Kovačić – P. Sučić, Baturina, Perišić – Beljo 
 CZECHIA: Kinsky – Coufal, Zima, Vlček, Slama – Červ, Kral – Hopi, Sadilek, Kabongo – Hložek
